title: Big White ski patrollers get top awards
excerpt: The awards were given by the Canadian Ski Patrol's Pacific South Division
content:
Published 9:59 am Tuesday, September 15, 2026

Big White ski patrollers are being recognized as some of the best in the province.

Recently, Big White Ski Resort and the Canadian Ski Patrol Ogopogo Zone (CSPOZ) received two awards from the Canadian Ski Patrol’s Pacific South Division.

The CSPOZ were given the Division Outstanding Zone Award, which celebrates “the hard work, dedication and achievements of its volunteer patrol team.”

As part of the the Canadian Ski Patrol’s Pacific South Division, the CSPOZ is one of six zones in southern B.C.

The CSPOZ has volunteers that operate in Big White Ski Resort, Phoenix Mountain Ski Area and Telemark Nordic Club.

The resort on the other hand received the Division Appreciation Award. It was given to them due to the resort’s “ongoing support of the Canadian Ski Patrol at the local, regional, national and international levels.”

Earlier this year, Big White hosted the 25th Congress of the International Federation of Ski Patrols which saw over 150 delegates from 12 different countries attend. The event was part of the reason the resort was given the award.

“The people behind the Canadian Ski Patrol give their time, expertise and care to help keep mountain communities safe, and we are incredibly proud to support them,” said Michael J. Ballingall, senior vice-president of Big White Ski Resort. “Hosting the FIPS World Congress gave us the opportunity to welcome patrol leaders from around the world and celebrate the skill and professionalism of this community. To receive this recognition alongside the Ogopogo Zone makes it especially meaningful, because its volunteers are an important part of the Big White family.”

In a release, the resort said the CSPOZ held its initial volunteer open house on Sept. 10. Training classes begin Tuesday, on Sept. 15, and will be held on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 6 p.m. to 9:30 p.m.

“Big White Ski Resort extends its congratulations and appreciation to the CSPOZ volunteers for their continued service, professionalism and commitment to helping create a safe and welcoming mountain environment,” the resort said.
